question.text: Aravalli Long-Short Fund values an INR 100 par bond with a 12% annual coupon, 8 years to maturity, and a required return of 14%. Using PVA(14%,8)=4.639 and PV(14%,8)=0.351, what is the bond's value?

explanation.text: The Logic: Value = 12 * 4.639 + 100 * 0.351 = 55.67 + 35.10 = INR 90.77. Required return (14%) > coupon (12%), so the bond trades at a discount. Directly from Example 12.1. The Trap: INR 100 is par - correct only when coupon = YTM. INR 112 is undiscounted; INR 96 uses wrong annuity factor. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C and X-B test bond discount/premium relationships. VIII applies the same PV logic to futures fair value.
